source:
@@U02723@@
A difficult case, I admit. But listen to me. You must take this piece of charcoal and work your way up quite close to him. With the charcoal then you'll put a mark on him somewhere— arm, coat, shoulder, wherever, and at once he'll suffer the sweet pangs of remorse. Immediately, then, you must swallow the charcoal and let neither wine nor water touch your lips. This very night he'll be sighing at your door.

@@U02725@@
I trust it’s not poisonous?

@@U02727@@
(/ndignant.)

@@U02728@@
You will show respect where it’s due, madam! One must search far and wide for charcoal like this. It comes from a funeral pyre— an auto-da-fe—an activity we once engaged in more assiduously.

@@U02730@@
I’m in love, but they say I’m too young.

@@U02732@@
(Aside.)

@@U02733@@
I’m at wit’s end! Whom do I listen to next! Forget the sweet young things; older women will know how to appreciate you more.

@@U02734@@
(Others crowd around him.)
translation:
@@U02723@@
我承认，这是一个困难的案例。但听我说。你必须拿着这块木炭，慢慢靠近他。然后你会用木炭在他的某个地方留下一个记号——手臂、外套、肩膀，无论什么地方，他立刻就会遭受悔恨的甜蜜痛苦。然后，你必须立即吞下木炭，不要让酒或水接触你的嘴唇。今晚他就会在你家门口叹息。

@@U02725@@
我相信它没有毒？

@@U02727@@
（/愤怒。）

@@U02728@@
女士，您会在适当的时候表现出尊重！像这样的木炭，必须四处寻找。它来自火葬柴堆——一项我们曾经更孜孜不倦地从事的活动。

@@U02730@@
我恋爱了，但他们说我太年轻。

@@U02732@@
（旁边。）

@@U02733@@
我已经无计可施了！下一个我该听谁的！忘记那些甜蜜的年轻事；年长的女人会更懂得如何欣赏你。

@@U02734@@
（其他人围在他周围。）
